source_title: Patrick Stewart dies at 86: His three marriages, children, grandchildren
source_excerpt: Patrick Stewart, best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise, has died at the age of 86. While his illustrious career made him a celebrated name across generations, his personal life was marked by three marriages, two children, four grandchildren and candid reflections on the choices he made along the way.The actor was married to Sheila Falconer, Wendy Neuss and, most recently, musician Sunny Ozell. His marriage to Ozell brought him companionship in the later years of his life. However, Stewart was also open about the emotional toll of his earlier relationships, particularly the distance that developed between him and his children. In the years before his death, he spoke candidly about his regrets as a father and admitted that his dedication to acting had often come before his family.Patrick Stewart's first marriage to Sheila Falconer and their two childrenStewart married actress and dancer Sheila Falconer in 1966. The couple welcomed two children, Daniel, born in 1967, and Sophie, born in 1972. Their marriage lasted until 1990, when they divorced.The separation was a difficult chapter for the actor. In a 2023 conversation with USA Today, Stewart acknowledged his role in the breakdown of the marriage, saying, âMy first divorce was harrowing. And I was to blame for it being harrowing.âHis professional commitments also meant spending considerable time away from his family. While he worked in Los Angeles on Star Trek, Sheila remained in London, adding to the distance between them.Patrick Stewart's regret over his relationship with his childrenStewart's relationship with Daniel and Sophie remained complicated over the years, something he spoke about with unusual candour. In a 2023 interview with the Irish Independent, he described his relationship with his children as âpractically non-existentâ.The actor acknowledged that he had been separated from his children and admitted that his professional ambitions had affected his role as a father. Speaking about the distance between them, he said, âI always put my acting work first, before my family.âHe also reflected on how he could have handled fatherhood differently. âI could've done better as a parent, when my kids were little. I was just obsessed with my work and everything else took second place,â he admitted.Stewart spoke about the emotional weight of the estrangement, saying that ânot a dayâ went by without him feeling the pain of the situation. He also acknowledged that his own choices had contributed to the relationship he shared with his children as adults.His comments offered a deeply personal insight into the sacrifices he believed he had made in pursuit of his acting career. Despite his success, the actor continued to express sadness over the distance from Daniel and Sophie.His bond with four grandchildrenWhile Stewart was candid about his strained relationship with his children, he spoke warmly about his four grandchildren. In his 2023 memoir, Making It So, he described them as remarkable and said he got on wonderfully with them.He also spoke about trying to approach his relationship with the younger generation differently, recognising that he could have done better when his own children were growing up.Daniel followed his father into acting and appeared alongside him in projects including Star Trek: The Next Generation, Death Train and Blunt Talk. Sophie, meanwhile, largely stayed away from the public eye, although she accompanied her father to a few high-profile events, including the 2002 premiere of Star Trek: Nemesis.Patrick Stewart's second marriage to Wendy NeussAfter his divorce from Falconer, Stewart married television producer Wendy Neuss in 2000. Neuss had worked on Star Trek: The Next Generation and was associated with the franchise's later projects.Their marriage lasted three years, with the couple divorcing in 2003. Stewart subsequently found love again, this time with musician Sunny Ozell.His marriage to Sunny Ozell and their 38-year age gapStewart married Sunny Ozell in 2013, when he was 73. Ozell was approximately 35 at the time, making their age difference around 38 years. Their relationship attracted attention because of the age gap, but the couple remained together for nearly 13 years.The two first met in 2008 at a restaurant in Brooklyn, where Ozell was working as a waitress. Their wedding took place in 2013 and was officiated by Stewart's longtime friend and X-Men co-star Ian McKellen.Stewart shared a photograph from the ceremony with the playful caption, âYes, married.â The couple continued to make public appearances together over the years, with Ozell by his side during the final chapter of his life.Stewart had also spoken about wanting his Star Trek: Picard character to find the kind of happiness he had found in his own life. He hoped Picard's story would end with the character alongside his wife at a vineyard, reflecting his belief that the character deserved lasting love.While Patrick Stewart's career brought him international recognition, his own reflections on family revealed a more personal and vulnerable side. He spoke openly about the mistakes he believed he had made, the distance from his children and the sadness that stayed with him.
